basic_information.name: Query Transformation & Routing
basic_information.creator: Multiple — Luyu Gao et al./CMU (HyDE, 2022), Google DeepMind (Step-Back Prompting, 2023), Zackary Rackauckas/Infineon Technologies (RAG-Fusion, 2024), LangChain (MultiQueryRetriever), LlamaIndex (Sub-Question Query Engine, Query Transform modules), Aurelio AI (Semantic Router library), Stanford NLP/DSPy (composable query transforms)
basic_information.description: Query Transformation & Routing is a family of advanced RAG patterns that modify, expand, decompose, or route user queries before retrieval to bridge the vocabulary gap between how users ask questions and how information is stored. Key techniques include HyDE (Hypothetical Document Embeddings — generating a hypothetical answer to use its embedding for retrieval), Multi-Query (generating 3-5 query variations to capture different perspectives of the user's intent), Step-Back Prompting (abstracting to a higher-level question for broader context retrieval), Query Decomposition (breaking complex multi-part questions into atomic sub-queries), RAG-Fusion (combining multi-query generation with Reciprocal Rank Fusion for reranking), and Semantic Routing (classifying queries to select the optimal retrieval pipeline or knowledge source). These techniques address the fundamental problem that naive single-query retrieval misses relevant documents due to vocabulary mismatch, query ambiguity, or complexity, and collectively can improve retrieval accuracy by 15-36% depending on domain and technique.
basic_information.release_date: HyDE paper: December 2022 (arXiv:2212.10496, published ACL 2023). Step-Back Prompting: October 2023 (arXiv:2310.06117). RAG-Fusion: February 2024 (arXiv:2402.03367). LangChain MultiQueryRetriever: available since LangChain v0.0.x (2023). LlamaIndex Sub-Question Query Engine: available since 2023. Semantic Router (Aurelio AI): first release 2024, active development through 2026. RAGRouter paper: May 2025 (arXiv:2505.23052). Query Decomposition for RAG (Exploration-Exploitation): October 2025 (arXiv:2510.18633). CompactRAG: February 2026 (arXiv:2602.05728).
basic_information.license: HyDE reference implementation: MIT (texttron/hyde on GitHub). Semantic Router: MIT. LangChain MultiQueryRetriever: MIT. LlamaIndex query transforms: MIT. NirDiamant/RAG_Techniques: open-source. DSPy: MIT. RAG-Fusion reference code: open-source. Framework-level implementations are generally MIT or Apache 2.0. The underlying techniques are published academic methods — no patent restrictions.

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Pipeline pattern — query transformation is a pre-retrieval processing stage inserted between user input and the retriever. Architecture variants: (1) Single-transform pipeline — one technique applied (e.g., HyDE generates hypothetical doc, embeds it, retrieves). (2) Multi-branch pipeline — Multi-Query or RAG-Fusion generate N query variants, run N parallel retrievals, then fuse results via RRF or union-dedup. (3) Sequential decomposition — Query Decomposition breaks query into sub-queries, retrieves for each sequentially or in parallel, aggregates answers. (4) Router-based — Semantic Router classifies query intent, routes to different retrieval backends (vector search, knowledge graph, web search, SQL). (5) Hybrid/adaptive — combines complexity classification with technique selection (simple queries pass through, complex queries get decomposition + multi-hop). All patterns add an LLM call or embedding lookup before retrieval, trading latency for accuracy.
technical_architecture.language: Python (primary — all major frameworks use Python). JavaScript/TypeScript (LangChain.js MultiQueryRetriever, LlamaIndex.ts). Semantic Router is Python-native. HyDE and RAG-Fusion reference implementations are Python. Framework integrations available for any language via REST APIs to LLM providers.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Query transformation is embedding-dimension-agnostic — it works with any embedding model. HyDE specifically generates a hypothetical document that is then embedded using whatever embedding model the pipeline uses (OpenAI text-embedding-3: 256-3072 dims, Cohere embed-v3: 1024, open-source BGE/E5: 384-1024). Semantic Router uses embeddings for route classification — supports OpenAI, Cohere, FastEmbed, and Hugging Face models. The transformed queries are embedded by the same model as normal queries.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: Query transformation does not change the indexing algorithm — it transforms the query before it hits the existing index. Compatible with all vector indexing methods: HNSW, IVF, DiskANN, flat, product quantization. HyDE's key insight is that hypothetical document embeddings are closer in vector space to relevant stored documents than the original short query embedding is. Multi-Query and RAG-Fusion run multiple queries against the same index. Semantic Router maintains a separate small index of route embeddings (typically kNN with cosine distance) for query classification.
technical_architecture.scalability: Query transformation adds per-query overhead but does not affect index scalability. Key scaling considerations: (1) HyDE: 1 additional LLM call per query (generating hypothetical document) + 1 additional embedding call. Can generate 5 hypothetical docs and average embeddings for better quality at 5x LLM cost. (2) Multi-Query: typically 3-5 LLM-generated variants = 3-5x retrieval operations, results merged via union. (3) RAG-Fusion: N queries x K retrieved docs, then RRF fusion — computation scales as O(N*K). (4) Query Decomposition: variable number of sub-queries, each requiring retrieval + potentially LLM synthesis. (5) Semantic Router: sub-millisecond classification using embedding similarity — negligible overhead. (6) Routing: classification step adds ~1-75ms depending on method (embedding similarity vs small LLM). All techniques can be parallelized — multi-query retrieval runs concurrent searches.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: These are pipeline-level patterns, not standalone services. Deployment follows the host framework: (1) LangChain/LlamaIndex: any Python environment, Docker, Kubernetes, serverless (AWS Lambda, Google Cloud Functions). (2) Semantic Router: pip install as a Python library, runs locally or in any cloud environment. (3) No-code platforms: Flowise, Langflow, Dify, and RAGFlow offer visual configuration of query transformation steps. (4) Cloud-managed: Google Vertex AI RAG Engine includes query transformation options. AWS Bedrock Knowledge Bases supports query decomposition. Azure AI Foundry supports routing. (5) Edge/on-device: lightweight routing (embedding-based) can run on edge with small models; LLM-based transforms require API calls or local LLM.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Query transformation enhances all retrieval methods: (1) Dense vector retrieval — HyDE bridges the vocabulary gap by generating a document-like embedding. Multi-Query improves recall by capturing multiple intent facets. (2) Sparse BM25/SPLADE — query expansion adds relevant keywords that BM25 can match. (3) Hybrid (dense+sparse) — RAG-Fusion combines results from multiple retrievers using Reciprocal Rank Fusion. (4) Knowledge graph — Semantic Routing can direct entity-heavy queries to graph retrieval. (5) Multi-source — Query Decomposition + routing can send sub-queries to different data sources (vector DB, SQL, web search, API). The techniques are retriever-agnostic and composable.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Query transformation is chunking-strategy-agnostic — it operates before the retrieval stage and works with any chunking approach. However, the choice of transformation interacts with chunking: (1) HyDE generates document-length text, which aligns better with larger semantic chunks than small fixed-size chunks. (2) Multi-Query can compensate for suboptimal chunking by retrieving from multiple perspectives. (3) Query Decomposition works well with document-structure-aware and hierarchical (RAPTOR) chunking since sub-queries can target different document sections. (4) Step-Back Prompting benefits from larger context chunks that capture foundational concepts.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Query transformation and reranking are complementary stages in an advanced RAG pipeline. The standard flow is: Query Transform -> Retrieve -> Rerank -> Generate. RAG-Fusion has built-in reranking via Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF), which combines ranked lists from multiple query variants using the formula score = sum(1/(rank + k)). Multi-Query retrieval results can be deduplicated and then reranked with cross-encoders. CompactRAG (2026) limits LLM calls to exactly two per query (decomposition + synthesis) and uses lightweight relevance filtering between retrieval rounds, acting as an implicit reranking step.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Query transformation techniques are primarily text-focused but extending to multimodal: (1) Text queries can be routed to multimodal retrievers (image search, table extraction) via Semantic Routing. (2) HyDE can theoretically generate hypothetical captions for image retrieval. (3) HM-RAG (Hierarchical Multi-Agent Multimodal RAG, 2025) uses a Decomposition Agent to rewrite and decompose questions, then routes to multi-source retrieval including text, graph, and web sources. (4) LlamaIndex supports multimodal query engines where query decomposition can target different modalities. Fully multimodal query transformation (e.g., transforming an image query) remains an active research area.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: Query transformation integrates with Graph RAG through routing: (1) Semantic Routing can detect entity-relationship queries and route them to a knowledge graph retriever instead of vector search. (2) Query Decomposition can break a complex question into sub-queries, some targeting the knowledge graph (entity lookups, relationship traversals) and others targeting vector search (semantic similarity). (3) Step-Back Prompting can generate abstract questions that map well to ontology-level graph queries. (4) HM-RAG (2025) explicitly combines graph-based retrieval with vector and web retrieval through a multi-agent decomposition architecture.
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Query transformation indirectly improves citation quality by retrieving more relevant source documents. Multi-Query and RAG-Fusion increase recall, providing more candidate sources for citation. Query Decomposition enables per-claim sourcing — each sub-query's retrieved documents can be cited independently for each part of the answer. Semantic Routing to authoritative data sources (e.g., routing financial queries to verified databases) improves citation reliability. No built-in citation generation — this is handled by downstream LLM generation with the retrieved context.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Query transformation helps optimize context window usage in several ways: (1) Better retrieval precision means fewer irrelevant documents in the context, using tokens more efficiently. (2) RAG-Fusion's RRF reranking promotes the most relevant documents to the top, allowing truncation of lower-ranked results. (3) Query Decomposition breaks a complex query into focused sub-queries, each retrieving a smaller, targeted context rather than one large unfocused retrieval. (4) CompactRAG (2026) specifically addresses token overhead — the main LLM is invoked only twice per query (decomposition + synthesis), making LLM usage independent of reasoning hop depth. (5) Routing simple queries to fast single-hop retrieval avoids unnecessarily large context windows.

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: Query transformation adds latency due to extra LLM calls: (1) HyDE: +200-800ms for hypothetical document generation (1 LLM call) + embedding. With 5 hypothetical docs: +1-4s. (2) Multi-Query: +200-500ms for query variant generation (1 LLM call) + N parallel retrievals. (3) RAG-Fusion: similar to Multi-Query + <1ms for RRF computation. (4) Step-Back Prompting: +200-500ms for abstraction query generation. (5) Query Decomposition: +300-1000ms depending on number of sub-queries generated. (6) Semantic Router (embedding-based): <1ms classification overhead. (7) LLM-based routing: +50-200ms for a small classification LLM call. Production query-adaptive routing systems achieve 80-120ms for simple queries (single-hop) and 400-800ms for complex queries (multi-hop), with P50 latency reductions of ~35% versus static retrieval strategies.
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: Throughput depends heavily on the LLM used for transformation: (1) API-based LLM transforms (GPT-4, Claude): limited by API rate limits and concurrent request handling. (2) Self-hosted small LLMs for routing (Phi-2, Llama 2-7B): hundreds to thousands of classifications per second on GPU. (3) Embedding-based routing (Semantic Router): thousands of classifications per second — negligible overhead. (4) Multi-Query and RAG-Fusion multiply retrieval throughput requirements by N (number of generated queries). (5) Parallelization is key — Multi-Query retrievals can run concurrently, bringing wall-clock throughput close to single-query. CompactRAG reduces LLM calls to exactly 2 per query regardless of complexity, making throughput predictable.
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: HyDE: significant improvements on BEIR benchmarks — outperforms unsupervised dense retrieval on 11/11 BEIR datasets (from the original paper). Step-Back Prompting: up to 36% improvement in information retrieval accuracy (Google DeepMind), 27 percentage point gain on TimeQA when combined with RAG. Multi-Query: improves recall by 10-25% through broader coverage of user intent. RAG-Fusion: ~7% improvement over HyDE alone, ~2.55% over single-query RAG-Fusion baseline on complex multi-hop problems (MQRF-RAG study). Query Decomposition: 35% gain in document-level precision, 15% increase in alpha-NDCG (exploration-exploitation approach, arXiv:2510.18633). Query-Adaptive Routing: 8% answer accuracy improvement + 35% latency reduction + 28% LLM cost reduction in production enterprise systems.
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: BEIR (HyDE): Contriever-HyDE outperforms Contriever on all BEIR datasets without any relevance labels. Step-Back (Google DeepMind): tested on MMLU Physics, Chemistry, TimeQA, MuSiQue — consistent gains over chain-of-thought and baseline prompting. RAG-Fusion: evaluated via RAGElo automated Elo-based framework (arXiv:2406.14783). CompactRAG (2026): tested on HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, MuSiQue — reduces LLM calls while maintaining accuracy. Comprehensive RAG survey (arXiv:2506.00054) covers query transformation techniques across multiple benchmarks. No single unified benchmark exists for comparing all query transformation techniques — each paper evaluates on different datasets.

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: LangChain: MultiQueryRetriever (built-in), HypotheticalDocumentEmbedder class for HyDE, query transformation chains, routing via RunnableBranch and RunnablePassthrough. LlamaIndex: Sub-Question Query Engine, QueryTransform modules (HyDE, DecomposeQueryTransform, StepDecomposeQueryTransform), RouterQueryEngine for semantic routing, query transform cookbook documentation. Haystack: HyDE integration documented in official docs (HypotheticalDocumentEmbedder component). DSPy: composable query transformation as DSPy modules, optimizable with DSPy's compiler. Flowise/Langflow: visual query transformation nodes in no-code builders. NirDiamant/RAG_Techniques: reference notebooks for all major techniques (query_transformations.ipynb, HyDe.ipynb, fusion_retrieval.ipynb).
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Query transformation works with any LLM for the generation step: OpenAI GPT-4/4o (most commonly used in tutorials and reference implementations), Anthropic Claude, Google Gemini, Mistral, open-source models (Llama, Phi, Qwen). For HyDE, the hypothetical document quality depends on the LLM's domain knowledge — stronger models produce better hypothetical documents. For routing, smaller specialized models work well: Phi-2 and Llama 2-7B achieve 85-92% accuracy at <1ms cost. Semantic Router works with any embedding provider: OpenAI, Cohere, FastEmbed, Hugging Face models.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Emerging. Query transformation is typically embedded within RAG pipelines rather than exposed as standalone MCP tools. Some RAG platforms (Dify, R2R) that offer MCP endpoints include query transformation as part of their pipeline configuration. Claude Desktop and MCP-compatible agents can invoke query transformation through tool-use APIs wrapping LangChain or LlamaIndex. No dedicated MCP server specifically for query transformation exists as of February 2026.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: Query transformation is data-source-agnostic — it operates on the query before it reaches any data source. However, Semantic Routing enables intelligent connector selection: route financial queries to Bloomberg API, code queries to GitHub search, general knowledge queries to vector DB, structured data queries to SQL databases. LlamaIndex RouterQueryEngine can route to different query engines backed by different data sources (Pinecone, Weaviate, Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL, web search). LangChain routing chains support conditional retriever selection based on query classification.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Query transformation steps can be traced via: LangSmith (LangChain) — logs each query transformation step, generated queries, retrieved docs per variant, and fusion results. Langfuse — supports tracing multi-step RAG pipelines including query transforms. Arize Phoenix — monitors retrieval quality before/after transformation. Key metrics to track: number of query variants generated, retrieval overlap between variants (low overlap = good diversity), RRF score distributions, routing accuracy (% correctly classified queries), latency breakdown per transformation step. OpenTelemetry spans can wrap each transformation step for custom observability.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Query transformation adds per-query LLM costs on top of base RAG pipeline costs: (1) HyDE: 1 additional LLM call (~100-500 output tokens for hypothetical document). At GPT-4o pricing ($2.50/1M input, $10/1M output): ~$0.001-0.005 per query. (2) Multi-Query: 1 LLM call generating 3-5 query variants (~50-150 output tokens): ~$0.0005-0.002 per query. (3) RAG-Fusion: same as Multi-Query + negligible RRF computation. (4) Step-Back: 1 LLM call for abstraction (~20-50 tokens): ~$0.0002-0.001 per query. (5) Query Decomposition: 1 LLM call (~100-300 tokens): ~$0.001-0.003 per query. (6) Semantic Router: no LLM cost — uses embedding similarity only. One-time setup cost for route embeddings. (7) LLM-based routing: 1 small LLM call for classification (~20-50 tokens): ~$0.0001-0.0005 per query. Costs scale linearly with query volume.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: All query transformation techniques are free to implement using open-source frameworks (LangChain, LlamaIndex, DSPy — all MIT license). Semantic Router: MIT license, fully free. NirDiamant/RAG_Techniques: free reference implementations. The only cost is the underlying LLM API calls. Using free/open-source LLMs (Llama, Mistral, Phi) eliminates API costs entirely. Semantic Router with local embeddings (FastEmbed) runs with zero API cost.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: At 1M queries/day with GPT-4o: (1) HyDE: ~$1,000-5,000/day additional LLM cost. (2) Multi-Query (3 variants): ~$500-2,000/day + 3x retrieval cost. (3) RAG-Fusion: same as Multi-Query. (4) Semantic Routing only: ~$0/day (embedding-based). (5) Query-Adaptive Routing (classify + conditional transform): saves 28% on LLM API costs by routing simple queries to cheaper/faster paths — net cost reduction despite added classification step. Using smaller models for transformation (GPT-4o-mini at $0.15/1M input): costs drop 10-20x. Self-hosted Llama or Phi for transforms: only GPU compute cost (~$2-3/hour for inference server). CompactRAG approach (exactly 2 LLM calls per query regardless of complexity) provides predictable cost ceiling.
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Query transformation TCO = transformation LLM cost + additional retrieval cost (for multi-query) + base RAG pipeline cost. Key TCO insight: despite adding cost, query transformation often reduces total pipeline TCO because: (1) Better retrieval precision means fewer irrelevant tokens sent to the expensive generation LLM. (2) Routing simple queries to fast paths saves 28-40% on LLM costs. (3) Fewer hallucinations reduce human review costs. (4) Higher quality answers reduce follow-up query volume. Net effect: enterprises report 20-40% efficiency gains when implementing query-adaptive routing versus static retrieval. Engineering investment: 1-4 weeks to implement, minimal ongoing maintenance once configured.

adoption_and_market.market_position: Query transformation has become a standard best practice in production RAG systems (2025-2026). It is not a product but a family of techniques implemented across all major RAG frameworks. Adoption hierarchy: (1) Multi-Query and Query Rewriting — most widely adopted, built into LangChain and LlamaIndex as first-class components. (2) Semantic Routing — rapidly growing, driven by enterprise need for multi-source RAG. (3) HyDE — well-known but selective adoption due to latency overhead. (4) RAG-Fusion — growing adoption for high-precision use cases. (5) Step-Back Prompting — niche adoption, mainly for knowledge-intensive domains. (6) Query-Adaptive Routing — emerging as enterprise standard (2026), with production systems reporting 35% latency cuts and 8% accuracy gains.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: Query transformation techniques are embedded in production systems across industries: Google Vertex AI RAG Engine (includes query transformation options), AWS Bedrock Knowledge Bases (supports query decomposition), Azure AI Foundry (model routing), Notion AI (uses Cohere-powered retrieval with query optimization), Databricks Mosaic AI (query routing in RAG agents). Enterprise RAG platforms like Glean, Vectara, and Squirro implement query transformation as core pipeline components. 52% of enterprises using GenAI now run AI agents in production (Google Cloud 2025 ROI Report), many leveraging query routing for multi-source retrieval. adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Query transformation techniques complement rather than compete with each other. The landscape is better understood as a toolkit: (1) Simple query rewriting — baseline, nearly universal. (2) Multi-Query/RAG-Fusion — compete as multi-perspective approaches; RAG-Fusion adds RRF reranking. (3) HyDE — unique approach (hypothetical doc generation), no direct competitor. (4) Step-Back — competes with chain-of-thought for reasoning-intensive queries. (5) Query Decomposition — competes with agentic multi-hop approaches (CRAG, Self-RAG). (6) Routing — Semantic Router (Aurelio AI) vs LangChain RunnableBranch vs LlamaIndex RouterQueryEngine vs vLLM Semantic Router vs RAGRouter (academic). Key trend: convergence toward adaptive systems that automatically select the right transformation based on query complexity (query-adaptive RAG routing).

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Query transformation is essential for any startup building RAG-powered products. Recommended adoption path: (1) Day 1 (MVP, 1-3 engineers): Start with simple query rewriting and Semantic Routing for multi-source retrieval. Use LangChain MultiQueryRetriever — 5 lines of code, immediate 10-25% recall improvement. Zero infrastructure cost if using embedding-based routing. (2) Growth stage (3-10 engineers, product-market fit confirmed): Add HyDE for domain-specific terminology gaps (legal, medical, technical). Implement RAG-Fusion for high-stakes queries requiring precision. Build query-adaptive routing to optimize cost/latency. (3) Scale stage (10+ engineers, high query volume): Deploy CompactRAG-style patterns to minimize LLM calls. Fine-tune routing classifiers on production query logs. Implement multi-stage transformation pipelines. Best use cases: customer support (routing to FAQ vs knowledge base vs escalation), enterprise search (routing across data sources), legal/medical RAG (HyDE for terminology bridging), e-commerce (query decomposition for complex product queries).
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Build (recommended for most): Query transformation techniques are well-documented, open-source, and straightforward to implement. LangChain and LlamaIndex provide production-ready components. Semantic Router is a pip install away. Total implementation time: 1-5 days for basic techniques, 2-4 weeks for full adaptive routing. Buy when: using a managed RAG platform (Vectara, Glean, Google Vertex AI, AWS Bedrock) — these include query transformation as built-in features. No need to reimplement. Hybrid approach: use open-source frameworks for transformation logic, paid LLM APIs for the underlying generation calls. Key insight: the techniques themselves are free — the cost is only in LLM inference and engineering time.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: Single technique (Multi-Query or HyDE): 1-3 days for POC, 1-2 weeks for production with error handling, fallbacks, and monitoring. Semantic Routing: 2-5 days for POC including route definition, 1-2 weeks for production. RAG-Fusion pipeline: 3-7 days for POC, 2-3 weeks for production with RRF tuning. Query-Adaptive Routing (full system): 2-4 weeks for POC with complexity classifier + multiple pipelines, 4-8 weeks for production with monitoring, A/B testing, and optimization. Query Decomposition for multi-hop: 1-2 weeks for POC, 3-6 weeks for production (most complex due to sub-query orchestration and answer synthesis).
key_lessons: Start with Multi-Query — it is the simplest, lowest-risk query transformation with the broadest benefit. Generating 3-5 query variants and merging results improves recall 10-25% with just 1 additional LLM call and minimal latency overhead. LangChain's MultiQueryRetriever requires only 5 lines of code to integrate.

Use Semantic Routing to avoid over-engineering. Not every query needs the same retrieval strategy. Embedding-based routing (Aurelio Semantic Router) classifies queries in <1ms with zero LLM cost, directing simple factual queries to fast vector search and complex analytical queries to multi-hop retrieval. This alone can cut latency 35% and LLM costs 28%.

HyDE is powerful but selective — use it where vocabulary mismatch is the bottleneck, not everywhere. HyDE excels in domain-specific RAG (legal, medical, scientific) where user queries use different terminology than stored documents. For general-purpose RAG with well-written queries, Multi-Query often outperforms HyDE at lower cost and latency.

Query Decomposition is critical for multi-part questions but adds significant complexity. Each sub-query requires its own retrieval and potentially its own synthesis step. Use CompactRAG-style patterns (exactly 2 LLM calls: decomposition + final synthesis) to keep costs predictable. Start with simple decomposition before building full agentic multi-hop systems.

Measure transformation impact rigorously before scaling. Track: retrieval overlap between query variants (low overlap = good diversity), percentage of queries where transformation changes the top retrieved document, end-to-end answer quality with and without transformation, latency and cost overhead per technique. A transformation that never changes retrieval results is wasted compute.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Yes — several no-code platforms support query transformation: Flowise (visual RAG builder with query transformation nodes), Langflow (drag-and-drop query transformation and routing components), Dify (configurable query rewriting and routing in pipeline builder), RAGFlow (query transformation as pipeline step), Google Vertex AI RAG Engine (UI-configurable query transformation). Flowise and Langflow are open-source and specifically designed for visual RAG pipeline construction, processing complex RAG workflows with query routing support.

Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects) — routing as an architectural decision in RAG pipeline design, build-vs-buy analysis for query transformation. confidence.data_quality: High — based on peer-reviewed papers (HyDE at ACL 2023, Step-Back Prompting from Google DeepMind, RAG-Fusion arXiv), official framework documentation (LangChain, LlamaIndex, Haystack), production benchmark reports (query-adaptive routing 35% latency reduction), and comprehensive survey papers (arXiv:2506.00054, arXiv:2507.18910). confidence.cross_reference: HyDE performance verified across: original paper (ACL 2023, Gao et al.), Zilliz implementation guide, Haystack official documentation, LangChain HypotheticalDocumentEmbedder docs. Step-Back Prompting results confirmed via Google DeepMind paper and multiple independent reproductions. RAG-Fusion validated via RAGElo benchmark framework (arXiv:2406.14783). Query-adaptive routing benchmarks confirmed across ASCII News report, ragaboutit.com analysis, and multiple enterprise case studies. Multi-Query improvements documented in LangChain blog, Full Stack Retrieval community, and NirDiamant reference implementations.
confidence.caveats: Performance gains vary significantly by domain, query distribution, and data quality — the 15-36% improvement range spans best-case scenarios. HyDE can degrade performance if the LLM generates hallucinated hypothetical documents (garbage in, garbage out). Multi-Query adds N-fold retrieval cost that may not be justified for simple queries. Step-Back Prompting's 36% improvement was measured on specific Google DeepMind benchmarks and may not generalize. No single unified benchmark exists for comparing all query transformation techniques — each paper evaluates on different datasets. The field is evolving rapidly — new techniques like CompactRAG (Feb 2026) and DMQR-RAG continue to emerge. Latency numbers are approximate and heavily dependent on LLM provider, model size, and infrastructure. Enterprise adoption statistics (52% running agents in production) may include simple routing that predates formal query transformation techniques.
confidence.security_posture: Query transformation introduces specific security considerations: (1) Prompt injection via query — transformed queries may amplify injected instructions if the user's input contains adversarial prompts. Multi-Query generation could multiply the attack surface by generating N variants of a malicious query. (2) Hypothetical document leakage — HyDE's generated documents may contain hallucinated sensitive information from the LLM's training data, which then gets embedded and used for retrieval. (3) Routing manipulation — adversarial queries could be crafted to misroute to unintended backends (e.g., bypassing access controls by routing to a less-restricted data source). (4) Query logging exposure — transformed queries contain LLM-generated content that may be stored in logs, creating data residency concerns. Mitigations: input validation before transformation, output filtering after retrieval, routing access control lists, and treating transformed queries with the same security scrutiny as user inputs. Defense frameworks reducing attack success from 73.2% to 8.7% apply to the full pipeline including query transformation stages.
